g.text: Active: new sessions may start on this provider · on
The login happens in the browser: approve on claude.ai, then paste the code it shows back here.
Settings · Provider › Provider tab (API token mode)
Active: new sessions may start on this provider · off
opencode authenticates with an API key per service and has no login of its own.
OK: the endpoint offers 12 models; they are in the Models tab, save to keep them
Test probes the endpoint and token as the form holds them, no save needed, and puts the endpoint's models in the Models tab.
One model per line; empty offers the CLI's own list.
One effort per line; empty offers the CLI's own.
Check usage reads the account and its quota again rather than the server's last answer.
Reference: briareus-windows. Other clients match this structure, differing only as noted here.
Each provider row in the sidebar has a dot and tag chips: the binary, 'inactive', 'own login', 'custom endpoint'. A new unsaved row reads 'New provider' / 'not saved yet'.

Binary choices: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex), grok (Grok), opencode. Mode (Login / API token) is offered only for binaries that support both; grok shows 'grok signs in with its own login; it takes no API token.'
When codex logs in, the device code appears with a Copy button. When claude logs in, a 'Code from the browser' field and a Finish button appear.
The Status tab exists only once the provider is saved. Its quota bars use the labels the provider sends back.
A new provider shows only Save; ⧉ clone and 🗑 delete are icon-only buttons.
Region names (sidebar, canvas, raise, sunken) are the theme.* roles; widths and margins are layout.* in tokens/. Greys only, on purpose.
